Subject: Dedicated pool renewal — early capacity check for Q3 expansion

Hi Emily,

As we approach your July renewal, wanted to start alignment on the Dedicated capacity piece you mentioned in the Q2 review. You noted higher batch QPS for ranking and an upcoming pilot that will increase average sequence length — both of which impact GPU sizing.

Can you confirm the revised QPS and token-per-request assumptions for July–Sep? If you can share a short forecast (week-by-week or monthly) I’ll run this past infra and come back with recommended reserved pool sizing and a 99th-percentile latency target we can include in the contract.

We can support an add-on of reserved GPUs or a burst tier depending on whether you prefer cost predictability or short-term headroom.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate pricing and any SLA language with Lauren and Marissa once we have numbers.

— Rishi

Thanks Rishi — confirmed and appreciative of the heads up. Below is what we expect for the July–September window:

- Baseline (June avg): 450 QPS, ~28 tokens/request (mostly short chat)
- July (pilot ramp): 750 QPS, 42 tokens/request (ranking + longer prompts)
- August (steady state): 1,050 QPS, 46 tokens/request
- September (peak estimate): 1,400 QPS, 50 tokens/request (marketing campaign + inference bursts)

We can attach the spreadsheet of request counts per route; Alex included an anonymized sample in the attachment. Our main ask: keep 99th latency under 300ms for generation routes at steady state.

If you can propose GPU counts and a reserved-pool configuration that hits that SLO and shows cost math, procurement can review and start the renewal paperwork.

Best,

Forwarding Nebula's forecast — raising this for pricing and infra sizing. Key asks: 99p < 300ms at steady state (Aug) and capacity to handle September peak.

Notes: EMILY'S FORECAST -> Jul 750 QPS / Aug 1,050 QPS / Sep 1,400 QPS; avg tokens up to 50. They currently use our c5-generation-variant (FP16) with KV cache enabled.

Connor — can you run a quick back-of-envelope GPU recommendation for their model family (gpt-like 30B class) and propose: 1) reserved pool GPUs for steady-state; 2) burst pool size; 3) suggested 99p SLO headroom and whether we need to propose a performance-tiered price?

Lauren & Marissa — I expect this to be an upsell (annual commit) so please prep pricing guidance and any concessions (one-time setup credit?). Marissa, can you draft a clean appendix for the renewal that calls out the capacity guarantee and preemption policy?

Thanks — Rishi
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool renewal — early capacity check for Q3 expansion

Quick run (assumptions detailed below) — recommendations attached (Redwood_reserved_pool_proposal_v2.pdf):

Assumptions
- Model class: 30B dense transformer, FP16 runtime, KV cache used across chat sessions
- Average tokens/request (Aug steady): 46; peak sequence length considered 1024 for bursts
- Effective QPS scaling: batching efficiency improves with bigger pools; 16-token batches typical
- Target SLO: 99th percentile latency <= 300ms for generation routes

Steady-state (August) recommendation
- Provision 18 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool. Rationale: with KV caching and continuous batching, 18 GPUs sustain ~1,200–1,400 inference QPS for 30B class with 46 tokens/request while keeping 99p ~250ms. We pick 18 to provide ~8–12% headroom over the expected 1,050 QPS to cover model variance.

Burst capacity
- Add a burst pool of 6 x A100-80GB (on-demand reserved at lower-commit discount) to absorb September peak up to 1,400 QPS. Bursts will be prioritized via routing policy; if burst exhausted, routing falls back to a compatible 13B quantized variant (pre-warmed).

Contract implications
- Term: propose 12-month renewal with a Q3 ramp addendum. Pricing tier: reserved 18 GPUs + 6 GPU burst option priced as reserved-with-burst for predictable monthly commitment.
- SLO: include 99p latency target of 300ms with penalty thresholds only if sustained >72 hours (standard rolling window).

Attachments: cost breakdown per-GPU, expected token tokens/month estimates (from Nebula spreadsheet), and an operations playbook for cache warming during rollout.

If we want to be more conservative, move to 22 GPUs reserved which would keep 99p ~220ms and remove the need for a large burst pool; tradeoff is higher monthly commit.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
From: Emily Jones <emily.jones@nebula.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool renewal — early capacity check for Q3 expansion

Thanks everyone — that recommendation is helpful and matches our internal expectations. We prefer the 18 + 6 burst configuration as a balance of predictability and cost. Procurement will start paperwork against the 12-month term with the Q3 ramp addendum; please send a redlined SOW and a purchase-ready quote.

Two quick asks before we sign:
1) Can you include explicit language about pre-warmed quantized fallback (13B) and the routing priority during burst exhaustion?
2) We need a one-week trial window post-cutover where we can validate 99p without penalties (to cover the campaign onboarding).

If those are acceptable we'll route to DocuSign this week.

Emily Jones
Head of Product, Nebula AI
emily.jones@nebula.ai
